# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Chen_2017_TB_MTP_rifampicin_mouse"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Chen_2017_TB_MTP_rifampicin_mouse"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-017-9508-2>

This is the single-drug **rifampicin** application of the Multistate
Tuberculosis Pharmacometric (MTP) model to an acute *M. tuberculosis* H37Rv
infection in C57BL/6 mice (Chen 2017, *J Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn*). It is a
different paper from the four-drug combination-therapy MTP-GPDI model in BALB/c
mice (Chen 2017, *CPT:PSP*; see `Chen_2017_TB_MTP_GPDI_mouse`).

# Population

Sixty C57BL/6 mice were intratracheally infected with *M. tuberculosis* H37Rv
(10^5 CFU per mouse) on Day 0. Twenty-five received oral rifampicin at 1.00,
2.83, 8.88, 26.4 or 98.0 mg/kg/day (five per dose) for eight days from Day 1
and were sacrificed on Day 9; twenty received 30 mg/kg/day for up to eight days
and were sacrificed in groups of five on Days 2, 3, 4 and 9; fifteen untreated
mice were sacrificed on Days 1, 9 and 18. The endpoint is colony-forming units
(CFU) in the homogenised lungs, with a lower limit of quantification of 10
CFU/lungs (21.6% of observations were below it and were handled by the NONMEM
M3 method).

No pharmacokinetics were sampled in this study. Rifampicin blood
concentrations are predicted from an earlier mouse population-PK model with
auto-induction (the population-PK-parameter approach), with every PK value held
fixed. No interindividual variability was estimated.

```{r population}
rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Chen_2017_TB_MTP_rifampicin_mouse"))$population
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` entry carries an in-file comment pointing to the Chen 2017 (or
upstream) source location. The table below collects them for reviewer use. The
PK block is fixed from the upstream mouse population-PK model; the MTP transfer
rates kSF/kFN/kSN/kNS are fixed from the in vitro Clewe 2016 fit; the growth,
F0, kFSlin and the three exposure-response relationships were estimated in this
study.

| Block | Parameter | Value | Units | Source |
|-------|-----------|-------|-------|--------|
| RIF PK | `lcl` | log(79.321) FIX | mL/h/kg | S2 $THETA(1); Methods 79.3 (Days 1-2) |
| RIF PK | `lcl_late` | log(131.911) FIX | mL/h/kg | S2 $THETA(2); Methods 132 (Days >=3) |
| RIF PK | `ltclchange` | log(48) FIX | h | S2 $PK IF(TIME.GE.48) |
| RIF PK | `lvc` | log(1249.14) FIX | mL/kg | S2 $THETA(3); Methods 1250 (dose > 1.02 mg/kg) |
| RIF PK | `lvc_lowdose` | log(2278.74) FIX | mL/kg | S2 $THETA(4); Methods 2280 (dose <= 1.02 mg/kg) |
| RIF PK | `lka_excess` | log(0.994) FIX | 1/h | S2 $PK TVKA = KE + THETA(5) |
| RIF PK | `lfdepot` | log(0.656) FIX | fraction | S2 $THETA(6); Methods 65.6% |
| MTP | `lf0` | log(331000) | CFU/lungs | Table 1 (treated mice), RSE 54.1% |
| MTP | `lf0_untreated` | log(8340) | CFU/lungs | Table 1 (untreated mice), RSE 8.7% |
| MTP | `lkg` | log(0.0333) | 1/h | Table 1, RSE 4.4% |
| MTP | `lkfslin` | log(2.96e-5) | 1/h^2 | Table 1, RSE 29.8%; Eq. 1 |
| MTP | `lksf` | log(6.042e-4) FIX | 1/h | Table 1 / S2 $THETA(12) (Clewe 2016, 0.0145/day /24) |
| MTP | `lkfn` | log(3.7375e-8) FIX | 1/h | Table 1 / S2 $THETA(11) (Clewe 2016, 0.897e-6/day /24) |
| MTP | `lksn` | log(7.75e-3) FIX | 1/h | Table 1 / S2 $THETA(13) (Clewe 2016, 0.186/day /24) |
| MTP | `lkns` | log(5.125e-5) FIX | 1/h | Table 1 / S2 $THETA(14) (Clewe 2016, 0.123e-2/day /24) |
| RIF effect | `lemax_fg_rif` | log(0.716) | fraction | Table 1 (FGImax), RSE 16.2%; Eq. 3 |
| RIF effect | `lec50_fg_rif` | log(0.0397) | ug/mL | Table 1 (FGIC50), RSE 50.2% |
| RIF effect | `gamma_fd_r` | 2.19 | unitless | Table 1 (sigmoidicity), RSE 7.2% |
| RIF effect | `lemax_fd_rif` | log(352) | 1/h | Table 1 (FDEmax), RSE 12.8%; Eq. 4 |
| RIF effect | `lec50_fd_rif` | log(212) | ug/mL | Table 1 (FDEC50), RSE 30.4% |
| RIF effect | `lksd_rif` | log(4.91e-3) | mL/(h*ug) | Table 1 (SDk), RSE 12.9%; Eq. 5 |
| Residual | `propSd` | sqrt(0.0235) FIX | fraction | S2 first $SIGMA 0.0235 FIX (PK records; upstream popPK) |
| Residual | `addSd` | sqrt(0.217) | log(CFU/lungs) | Table 1 (additive log-scale variance), RSE 12.0%; S2 second $SIGMA 0.216544 |

Equation references (recovered from the typeset equation GIFs and confirmed
against the S2 `$DES` block):

* Natural growth time-dependent transfer `kFS = kFSlin * t`: Eq. 1.
* Inhibition of fast-multiplying growth `IFG = FGImax * C / (FGIC50 + C)`: Eq. 3.
* Stimulation of fast-multiplying death
  `EFD = FDEmax * C^gamma / (FDEC50^gamma + C^gamma)`: Eq. 4.
* Stimulation of slow-multiplying death `ESD = SDk * C`: Eq. 5.
* Three-state ODE system for fast (F), slow (S), non-multiplying (N) bacteria:
  Eqs. 6-8. The CFU observation is `log(F + S)` (S2 `$ERROR`: `IPRED =
  LOG(A(3)+A(4))`); non-multiplying N bacteria do not form colonies on solid
  media.

# Virtual cohort and simulation

The model is deterministic and typical-value (no IIV, no dosing-level random
effects). Rifampicin is given once daily by oral gavage for eight days from Day
1 (`time = 24 h` after infection, `addl = 7`, `ii = 24 h`). The covariate
`TRT_RIFAMPICIN` selects the initial fast-multiplying inoculum (331000 CFU/lungs
treated vs 8340 untreated); `DOSE_LOW` selects the larger apparent volume used
for the single 1 mg/kg cohort.

```{r cohort}
# The model has two endpoints (Cc and log_cfu) and no random effects. The
# typical-value solve uses sigma = NA rather than zeroRe(), which crashes on
# models with more than one endpoint.
mod <- readModelDb("Chen_2017_TB_MTP_rifampicin_mouse")

# One arm: observation rows on an ODE state (cmt = "central") with dvid = 1;
# rxode2 returns the bacterial states, Cc and log_cfu at those times.
# Rifampicin is dosed into the depot once daily for 8 days.
make_arm <- function(id, dose_mgkg, obs_days, treated = TRUE) {
  low <- as.numeric(dose_mgkg > 0 && dose_mgkg <= 1.02)
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = id, time = obs_days * 24, amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central",
    dvid = 1L, ii = 0, addl = 0L
  )
  dose <- NULL
  if (dose_mgkg > 0) {
    dose <- data.frame(
      id = id, time = 24, amt = dose_mgkg, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot",
      dvid = NA_integer_, ii = 24, addl = 7L
    )
  }
  ev <- rbind(obs, dose)
  ev$TRT_RIFAMPICIN <- as.numeric(treated)
  ev$DOSE_LOW <- low
  ev[order(ev$time, -ev$evid), ]
}

# Day-9 dose-response cohorts (Fig. 3) plus natural growth (Fig. 4a) and the
# 30 mg/kg longitudinal arm (Fig. 2, right).
day9_grid <- c(0, 1, 2, 4, 9)
events <- bind_rows(
  make_arm(0L, 0, c(0, 1, 9, 18), treated = FALSE),
  make_arm(1L, 1.00, day9_grid),
  make_arm(2L, 2.83, day9_grid),
  make_arm(3L, 8.88, day9_grid),
  make_arm(4L, 26.4, day9_grid),
  make_arm(5L, 98.0, day9_grid),
  make_arm(6L, 30.0, c(0, 2, 3, 4, 9))
)
dose_label <- c(
  "0" = "Natural growth", "1" = "1.00 mg/kg", "2" = "2.83 mg/kg",
  "3" = "8.88 mg/kg", "4" = "26.4 mg/kg", "5" = "98.0 mg/kg", "6" = "30 mg/kg"
)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod, events,
  keep = c("TRT_RIFAMPICIN", "DOSE_LOW"),
  returnType = "data.frame", sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE,
  atol = 1e-14, rtol = 1e-12, maxsteps = 1e6
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    day = time / 24,
    arm = dose_label[as.character(id)],
    log10_cfu = log10(pmax(fbugs + sbugs, 1))
  )
```

# Replicate Figure S1 -- typical rifampicin PK

Rifampicin blood concentration over 24 h after the Day-8 dose, across the six
dose levels. The peak concentrations and their roughly dose-proportional
spacing reproduce the supplement Figure S1 (`1 -> ~0.3`, `2.83 -> ~1.3`,
`8.88 -> ~4`, `26.4 -> ~12`, `30 -> ~13`, `97.5 -> ~44` ug/mL).

```{r figure-s1-pk}
pk_arm <- function(dose_mgkg) {
  low <- as.numeric(dose_mgkg <= 1.02)
  obs <- data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = 192 + seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), amt = 0, evid = 0L,
    cmt = "central", dvid = 1L
  )
  dose <- data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = seq(24, 192, by = 24), amt = dose_mgkg, evid = 1L,
    cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_
  )
  ev <- rbind(obs, dose)
  ev$TRT_RIFAMPICIN <- 1
  ev$DOSE_LOW <- low
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    mod, ev[order(ev$time, -ev$evid), ],
    returnType = "data.frame", sigma = NA, useLinCmt = FALSE,
    atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-10, maxsteps = 1e6
  )
  s <- s[s$time >= 192, ]
  tibble(tad = s$time - 192, Cc = s$Cc, dose = dose_mgkg)
}

pk <- bind_rows(lapply(c(1.00, 2.83, 8.88, 26.4, 30.0, 97.5), pk_arm)) |>
  mutate(dose = factor(dose))

ggplot(pk, aes(tad, Cc, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_y_log10(name = "Predicted rifampicin blood concentration (ug/mL)") +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Time after dose (hours)", breaks = seq(0, 24, 6)) +
  labs(
    title = "Replicates Figure S1 of Chen 2017",
    colour = "Dose (mg/kg)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

pk_peaks <- pk |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  summarise(Cmax = max(Cc), .groups = "drop")
pk_peaks |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg/kg)" = dose, "Cmax (ug/mL)" = Cmax) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Peak rifampicin blood concentration by dose (Day 8).")
```

# Replicate Figure 4a -- natural growth

With no drug, the fast-multiplying state grows exponentially and the slow- and
non-multiplying populations follow from the transfer network. The total
culturable CFU/lungs rises from the untreated inoculum (log10 ~ 3.9) to ~9 by
Day 18, matching the Fig. 4a / Fig. 2 (left) observed medians of ~4.3, ~6.9 and
~9.1 at Days 1, 9 and 18.

```{r figure-4a-growth}
ng <- sim |> filter(arm == "Natural growth")

ggplot(ng, aes(day, log10_cfu)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "log10(CFU/lungs)", limits = c(3, 10)) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Time after infection (days)", breaks = c(1, 9, 18)) +
  labs(title = "Replicates Figure 4a of Chen 2017 (natural growth)") +
  theme_minimal()

ng |>
  select(day, fbugs, sbugs, nbugs, log10_cfu) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Day" = day, "F" = fbugs, "S" = sbugs, "N" = nbugs,
    "log10(F+S)" = log10_cfu
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 2),
    caption = "Natural-growth trajectory of the three bacterial states (CFU/lungs)."
  )
```

# Replicate Figure 3 -- Day-9 dose-response

The predicted Day-9 culturable CFU/lungs falls monotonically with increasing
rifampicin dose, reproducing the dose-response of Fig. 3 (observed medians
~6.8, ~5.2 and ~1.5 at 2.83, 8.88 and 26.4 mg/kg, with 30 and 97.5 mg/kg
driven below the LLOQ).

```{r figure-3-doseresponse}
d9 <- sim |>
  filter(id %in% 1:5, day == 9) |>
  mutate(dose_mgkg = c(1.00, 2.83, 8.88, 26.4, 98.0)[match(id, 1:5)])

ggplot(d9, aes(dose_mgkg, log10_cfu)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_log10(name = "Rifampicin dose (mg/kg/day)") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "log10(CFU/lungs) at Day 9") +
  labs(title = "Replicates Figure 3 of Chen 2017 (Day 9 after infection)") +
  theme_minimal()

d9 |>
  select(dose_mgkg, log10_cfu) |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg/kg)" = dose_mgkg, "log10(CFU/lungs) Day 9" = log10_cfu) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Day-9 culturable CFU/lungs by rifampicin dose.")
```

# Replicate Figure 2 (right) -- 30 mg/kg longitudinal decline

The 30 mg/kg arm, the only dose level with longitudinal sampling, declines from
Day 2 to below the LLOQ by Day 9.

```{r figure-2-longitudinal}
r30 <- sim |> filter(arm == "30 mg/kg", day > 0)

ggplot(r30, aes(day, log10_cfu)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "log10(CFU/lungs)") +
  scale_x_continuous(name = "Time after infection (days)", breaks = c(2, 3, 4, 9)) +
  labs(
    title = "Replicates Figure 2 (right) of Chen 2017 (rifampicin 30 mg/kg)",
    caption = "Dashed line: LLOQ = 10 CFU/lungs (log10 = 1)."
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Validation checks

This is a deterministic, typical-value mechanistic model, so the checks below
are exact (no stochastic cohort). They pin the structural behaviour against the
published figures.

```{r validation}
# 1. Natural growth rises monotonically to the observed Fig 4a medians.
ng_v <- ng |> arrange(day)
stopifnot(
  all(diff(ng_v$log10_cfu) > 0),
  abs(ng_v$log10_cfu[ng_v$day == 1] - 4.3) < 0.4,
  abs(ng_v$log10_cfu[ng_v$day == 9] - 6.9) < 0.4,
  abs(ng_v$log10_cfu[ng_v$day == 18] - 9.1) < 0.4
)

# 2. Day-9 dose-response is strictly decreasing across the five dose levels.
d9_v <- d9 |> arrange(dose_mgkg)
stopifnot(all(diff(d9_v$log10_cfu) < 0))

# 3. Day-9 predictions track the digitised Fig 3 medians for the quantifiable
#    cohorts (2.83 and 8.88 mg/kg).
stopifnot(
  abs(d9_v$log10_cfu[d9_v$dose_mgkg == 2.83] - 6.8) < 0.6,
  abs(d9_v$log10_cfu[d9_v$dose_mgkg == 8.88] - 5.2) < 0.6
)

# 4. 30 mg/kg declines over time and ends below the LLOQ by Day 9.
r30_v <- r30 |> arrange(day)
stopifnot(
  r30_v$log10_cfu[r30_v$day == 9] < r30_v$log10_cfu[r30_v$day == 2],
  r30_v$log10_cfu[r30_v$day == 9] < 1
)

# 5. Rifampicin Cmax rises monotonically with dose and the 1 mg/kg peak is sub-
#    ug/mL (Fig S1).
pk_v <- pk_peaks |> mutate(dose = as.numeric(as.character(dose))) |> arrange(dose)
stopifnot(
  all(diff(pk_v$Cmax) > 0),
  pk_v$Cmax[pk_v$dose == 1] < 1,
  abs(pk_v$Cmax[pk_v$dose == 97.5] - 44) < 8
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Population-PK-parameter (PPP) approach.** No rifampicin PK was measured in
  this study. The entire PK block is fixed from the upstream mouse population-PK
  model (Chen 2016, *Eur J Pharm Sci*) and reproduced inline as `fixed()`
  values; that upstream paper is not required because every value it
  contributes is carried here.
* **Elimination-anchored absorption.** The upstream PK reparameterises
  absorption as `ka = kel + 0.994 /h` (`lka_excess`), the standard NONMEM
  idiom enforcing `ka > kel`. Because `kel = CL/V` is itself stratified by the
  auto-induction time step and by the lowest-dose volume, `ka` takes several
  values, none of which is printed in the paper; the offset is therefore kept
  as a parameter rather than flattened to a single `ka`.
* **Auto-induction clearance step.** CL/F steps from 79.3 to 132 mL/h/kg at 48
  h after infection (`t >= exp(ltclchange)`), per the S2 `IF(TIME.GE.48)`
  branch. The model's time axis is time since infection, matching the dataset
  (the fast-multiplying inoculum is set at time 0 and the first dose is at
  24 h). The step therefore falls at the second dose. The Methods text and the
  Fig. 1 legend describe the lower clearance as applying on "Days 1-2", and the
  `$THETA` comments read "Days <= 2" / "Days >= 3"; those day labels number the
  dosing days of the upstream PK study, where a 48 h threshold falls at the
  third dose. The control stream is what produced the Table 1 estimates, so
  the 48 h step is encoded as written.
* **Lowest-dose volume.** The single 1.00 mg/kg cohort (at or below the
  1.02 mg/kg / 1020 ug/kg threshold) uses the larger apparent volume
  2278.74 mL/kg via `DOSE_LOW`; all higher doses use 1249.14 mL/kg.
* **Dose units.** Doses are entered in mg/kg and the apparent volume is in
  mL/kg, so `central / vc` is in mg/mL; the model multiplies by 1000 to express
  the rifampicin blood concentration `Cc` in ug/mL (= mg/L), the units of the
  exposure-response EC50 values.
* **CFU observation excludes the N state.** The culturable CFU is `log(F + S)`
  (S2 `$ERROR`), because non-multiplying bacteria do not form colonies on solid
  media. The `log_cfu` output is floored at 1 CFU to keep the log finite when
  drug effect drives the culturable total below one organism.
* **No inoculum of slow- or non-multiplying bacteria.** The data did not
  support S0 or N0, so both are 0 at infection (Chen 2017 Results); only the
  fast-multiplying inoculum F0 is non-zero, and it differs between treated
  (331000) and untreated (8340) mice.
* **Fixed transfer rates.** kSF, kFN, kSN and kNS are fixed to the in vitro
  Clewe 2016 estimates (per-day values divided by 24 to per-hour); only kFSlin
  was re-estimated as a time-dependent transfer in this mouse study.
* **No rifampicin effect on the N state.** An effect on non-multiplying
  bacteria was tested but not statistically significant (Chen 2017 Results),
  so none is encoded; the N state changes only through transfer.
* **Residual error scale.** Table 1 reports the estimated additive residual
  variance on the log scale as 0.217; with log-transform-both-sides this is the
  natural-log CFU scale, so `addSd = sqrt(0.217)`. The control stream also
  carries a fixed proportional error on the rifampicin concentration
  (`$SIGMA 0.0235 FIX`, applied only to PK records, of which this study had
  none); it is kept as `propSd = sqrt(0.0235)` on `Cc` so the PK layer remains
  complete.
* **Near-zero initial amounts.** The control stream initialises the depot,
  central, slow- and non-multiplying compartments at 1e-5 rather than 0 (a
  numerical convenience for the log of the CFU sum); the model starts them at
  0, which changes the culturable count by far less than one CFU.
* **No interindividual variability.** `$OMEGA 0 FIX` in the control stream; the
  model is typical-value only.
* **30 mg/kg Day-2 offset.** The typical-value prediction at the first
  longitudinal time point (Day 2) sits below the observed median (~3.4 vs ~4.1
  on the log10 scale); the decline shape to below the LLOQ by Day 9 and the
  Day-9 dose-response otherwise track the published figures.

# Errata

* No erratum, corrigendum or author correction was identified for this article
  via the EuropePMC `commentCorrectionList` (null) or a PubMed "erratum" search
  as of 2026-10-15.
* The final NONMEM control stream (Electronic Supplementary Material S2) was
  used alongside Table 1: it is the only source that specifies the PK block,
  the `ka = kel + offset` reparameterisation and the `IPRED = log(F + S)`
  observation. Two `$THETA` entries are initial estimates superseded by the
  published Table 1 finals (FDEmax 67.08 -> 352; FDEC50 98.50 -> 212); the
  Table 1 finals are used.
